subject: MAP: POC gatekeeper sprint — environment activation & peering timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Brenda Park <brenda.park@medisyst.com>; it@medisyst.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: POC gatekeeper sprint — environment activation & peering timeline

Hi Brenda / MediSyst IT team,

Thanks again for committing to the POC. Attaching the draft MAP sheet with proposed sprint milestones — goal is to have a production-like environment ready for workload testing by the end of week 2. To keep the MAP tight and avoid blockers, we need the following items completed or acknowledged this week: 

- Org setup: create a MediSyst org with an admin user for Redwood testing (email list in the attached MAP).
- API keys: request one scoped API key for the POC (read/generate) and a second key for ephemeral test runs. We attached an api-key-template.txt to speed your internal request.
- IP allowlist: please confirm the public egress IPs you can open, or provide a CIDR range for our peering endpoint. We recommend opening the four Redwood egress IPs in the MAP notebook.
- VPC peering: confirm network contact and preferred maintenance window; I attached a vpc-peering-request-form.pdf for your network team to fill.

Proposed timeline (high level):
1) This week (Sept 29–Oct 2): org + API key request submitted; initial IP allowlist entry confirmed.
2) Next week (Oct 5–9): VPC peering prep & security questionnaire completed.
3) Week of Oct 12: smoke tests, KV cache warm-up, endpoint validation.

Please let us know if any of those dates are infeasible and who should own the VPC peering form on your side. Vivek and Michael are on the thread for technical details.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this MAP so we can move to evaluation runs.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_v1_schedule.xlsx, vpc-peering-request-form.pdf, api-key-template.txt
From: Brenda Park <brenda.park@medisyst.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: MediSyst IT <it@medisyst.com>; Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@medisyst.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC gatekeeper sprint — environment activation & peering timeline

Hannah — thanks for the clear schedule and the forms. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side.

- Org setup: I will ask our security admin (Carlos) to create the org and add the admin user by EOD Friday (Oct 2).
- API keys: we will need the exact scope and TTL suggestions. Can you confirm the minimum privileges needed for the POC?
- IP allowlist: we prefer to provide CIDR ranges rather than opening per-IP. Our network policy requires a /28 or larger block.
- VPC peering: Carlos will own the peering form; he needs your side's VPC ID and the preferred peering window (we'd prefer weekday evening after 7pm PT).

Also — we have a SOC-2 questionnaire that must be referenced in any peering or key exchange. Please route the questionnaire to our security mailbox (security@medisyst.com).

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC gatekeeper sprint — environment activation & peering timeline

Brenda — good questions, quick technical clarifications from our side: 

- API key scope: for the POC we need Token:generate and Token:inspect scopes. TTL recommendations: 30 days for the long-lived test key, 24 hours for ephemeral test runs. If your policy requires short TTLs, we can support a handshake flow to rotate ephemeral keys programmatically.
- CIDR: Redwood's peering endpoint accepts a /28 or larger. If you can provide a /28, that works. If not, we can fall back to a small set of egress IPs (will be slightly more operationally involved).
- VPC ID: our peering VPC ID (host) will be rwd-infer-vpc-us-west-2 (we'll provide the full ARN in the peering ticket). Preferred maintenance window we can do 8pm–10pm PT on Tue/Wed; evening window is fine.

Action items for us: I'll upload the exact VPC details into the peering form and loop Carlos on the ticket. Priyom — can you drop the short script (curl) that Carlos can run to validate IP connectivity after peering?

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

On 2026-09-29 12:47, Brenda Park wrote:
> Hannah — thanks for the clear schedule and the forms. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from our side...

Date: 2026-09-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: POC gatekeeper sprint — environment activation & peering timeline

Carlos / Brenda — adding the security side and API-provisioning steps so the ticket has everything in one place: 

1) API keys
   - Fill api-key-template.txt with recipient email and intended scopes and send back to devops@medisyst.com.
   - We will generate keys and send them via the secure key exchange link (DocuSign-like token) — anticipated turnaround ~24 hours after request.

2) Security questionnaire
   - Link to REDWOOD SOC-2 questionnaire: https://redwood.internal/docs/soc2-questionnaire (please send completed questionnaire to security@redwood.ai).

3) VPC peering checklist
   - Complete vpc-peering-request-form.pdf and attach required subnet/CIDR and route-table entries.
   - We'll create a peering connection from rwd-infer-vpc-us-west-2; once you fill the form, we'll provision from our side and request your acceptance.

4) Post-peering validation
   - We'll share a short connectivity check (ICMP/TCP) and a scripted curl against a health endpoint. Vivek will share the script.

If you prefer, I can open a short tracker (JIRA INF-5821) and convert the MAP milestones into tickets so we can track progress daily.

Regards,
Michael Grant
Director, Technical Solutions | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai
